answer: Agents can make valuable actions count only after a stake has remained locked through a long horizon and the account has completed a sequence of independently checked tasks. A newcomer’s first actions carry little weight; reputation grows with consistent work, while proven fraud burns the stake and erases accumulated standing. This makes a fleet of disposable identities costly: each must tie up capital and repeat the voyage of earning trust, rather than gaining influence by sheer account count. A costly stake is a useful signal, not proof of a unique human.
